evals.name: flux-kustomization-not-ready
evals.prompt: In the homelab repo, a FluxKustomizationNotReady alert is firing for the local cluster and nothing new is deploying. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing it.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the gitops domain and the FluxKustomizationNotReady runbook, finds the head of the dependency chain first, uses read-only kubectl/flux inspection, and fixes via Git -> make validate -> make flux-push -> reconcile rather than kubectl apply.

assertions.text: Routes to docs/observability/runbooks/gitops/FluxKustomizationNotReady.md (or the runbook index), not an invented procedure
Finds the head of the dependency chain before touching the symptom wave, noting dependency '...' is not ready means upstream
Starts with read-only inspection (kubectl get kustomization -A | grep -v ' True ', flux get sources, make flux-status)
Does not kubectl apply/edit over Flux; fixes in Git then reconciles
Notes that Unknown/progressing states do not page and cold bring-up retries are transient

evals.name: service-5xx-cross-signal
evals.prompt: A homelab microservice is returning 5xx at the edge. How do I find the root cause?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the applications domain and the microservices investigation workflow, uses the metrics -> logs(trace_id) -> traces -> profiles correlation path, and keeps application code changes in the service repo.

assertions.text: Routes to docs/observability/runbooks/microservices investigation workflows
Uses the trace_id pivot from VictoriaLogs to VictoriaTraces and notes exemplars are not available (RFC-0014 D-14)
Verifies the signal is live and labels are current before concluding
Keeps handler/business-logic fixes in the owning *-service repo, treating docs/api as the contract truth

evals.name: cnpg-corruption-vs-availability
evals.prompt: Someone ran a bad migration on product-db and the data looks wrong. Should I fail over to the DR replica to recover?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes integrity from availability, refuses failover/promotion for corruption because the bad WAL already replicated, routes to emergency-recovery and PITR, and treats the recovery as IC-gated and approval-required.

assertions.text: Classifies this as an integrity incident, not availability
Explicitly does NOT fail over or promote, because HA/DR replicates the bad write
Routes to PITR to a new cluster via emergency-recovery.md
Treats recovery as incident-only, IC go/no-go, requiring explicit approval

evals.name: slo-burn-rate-routing
evals.prompt: An SLO burn-rate alert is paging for the order service in homelab. Which runbook do I open?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that burn-rate pages have no per-alert runbook tree and routes through slo-burn-rate-alerts.md to the owning service rather than a RED alert file.

assertions.text: Routes through docs/observability/alerting/slo-burn-rate-alerts.md
States burn-rate alerts have no per-alert runbook tree and must not be mapped onto a RED runbook file
Pivots to the owning service's RED runbook after the burn-rate doc

evals.name: cleanup-stale-debug-note
evals.prompt: Clean up the scattered debug and troubleshooting notes in the homelab database docs.
evals.expected_output: Applies the four-way retain/promote/move/remove disposition, checks current manifests before changing status claims, preserves dated evidence and planned/historical labels, stays scoped to the database docs, and reports index drift separately.

assertions.text: Classifies each note as retain-in-place / promote / move-to-evidence / remove
Preserves dated decision/incident/drill/verification evidence and planned/historical/known-gap labels still true
Checks the current manifest or source before changing any status claim
Stays scoped to the requested database docs and does not open a repo-wide rewrite
Reports index drift and deferred candidates separately rather than silently correcting them

evals.name: merged-but-not-live
evals.prompt: I merged a PR that changes a Temporal worker's env, but the pods on Kind still run the old value an hour later. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Routes to gitops-delivery, explains that Flux serves the artifact make flux-push built from the working tree (merging is not deploying), and verifies by reading the live object after make sync from an up-to-date tree; never kubectl apply over Flux.

assertions.text: States that merging to main does not deploy on Kind: Flux serves what make flux-push built from the working tree
Fixes with make sync / make flux-push from a tree containing the change, then reads the live object back
Does not kubectl apply or kubectl set env over Flux

evals.name: down-alert-silent
evals.prompt: A Deployment's metrics endpoint disappeared after a bad rollout, but its 'X is down' alert built on up == 0 never fired. Why?
evals.expected_output: Routes to observability-alerts, explains that up == 0 matches nothing once the target vanishes, and recommends an absent() half; verifies the signal exists before tuning thresholds.

assertions.text: Explains that up == 0 cannot match a target that is no longer scraped
Recommends adding an absent(up{...}) or absent(<signature metric>) half
Points at docs/platform/worker-autoscaling.md §4 or the alert lifecycle guide rather than inventing a procedure

evals.name: count-once-alert-never-fires
evals.prompt: Our new alert uses rate(checkout_failures_total[5m]) > 0 for a rare event, and it never fires even when the event happens. Why?
evals.expected_output: Routes to observability-alerts and the signal contract: a series born by the event has no earlier sample so rate() reads 0; use sum(increase(x[15m])) > 0 with for: 0m.

assertions.text: Explains that a series created by the event has no prior sample, so rate() stays 0
Recommends increase() over a window with for: 0m or a short for
Links docs/observability/alerting/alert-lifecycle-and-runbooks.md#2-define-the-signal-contract

evals.name: cdc-mirror-running-but-stale
evals.prompt: PeerDB shows every mirror as STATUS_RUNNING but the analytics page says data is stale. How do I tell what is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Routes to data-cdc-analytics, does not trust mirror status, checks pg_replication_slots.active and heartbeat age, and considers a recent primary restart or switchover (stale non-synced slots on the demoted primary).

assertions.text: States that mirrors report STATUS_RUNNING even while disconnected
Judges health by pg_replication_slots.active and heartbeat age
Mentions the demoted-primary stale-slot case after a switchover and routes to the CDC hub, read-only first

evals.name: kind-bringup-zfs-host
evals.prompt: make up on my workstation hangs: kubelet crash-loops with 'failed to get rootfs info' and the host starts swapping. Where do I look?
evals.expected_output: Routes to kubernetes-infra and setup prerequisites: the ZFS Docker root breaks kubelet 1.36/1.37 (keep the 1.35.8 pin) and an uncapped ZFS ARC starves Kind; asks the owner before any root-level change.

assertions.text: Identifies the kubelet 1.36/1.37 rootfs crash on a ZFS Docker root and the 1.35.8 pin
Checks zfs_arc_max / ARC size as the memory cause
Treats the ARC cap as a host change needing the owner's approval (root)

evals.name: checkout-503-fresh-kind
evals.prompt: On a freshly brought-up Kind cluster, every checkout confirm returns 503. Services are healthy. What should I check?
evals.expected_output: Routes to applications and the seed docs: a fresh Kind cluster has no demo data, so checkout fails closed; run make seed once, and make e2e-restock after load runs.

assertions.text: Explains that Kind is not seeded automatically, so product/inventory rows are missing
Recommends make seed (Kind-only guard) and make e2e-restock after load runs
Recognises 503 as checkout failing closed, not a service outage
